# LegalOS manual test data

Nineteen fully synthetic documents for manually testing LegalOS. All parties, people, CINs, PANs, GSTINs, bank accounts and phone numbers are made up (the GSTIN `24ABCDE1234F1Z5` is a placeholder; its check character is deliberately not valid). Dates are set around "today" = 27/28 Oct 2026, so deadlines in the notices are still live.

Workspaces: Contract Intelligence (CI), Legal Notice Center (LNC), Compliance Center (CC), Knowledge Hub (KH), Vendor Intelligence (VI).

Clause numbers below refer to the numbered clauses inside each file.

## 4. Vendors (for Vendor Intelligence GSTIN checks)

Real, publicly printed GSTINs of large listed companies. Only two are given because I could verify only these two by structure (state code + PAN + entity code + `Z` + check character, with the GSTIN check-digit algorithm re-computed and matching). I deliberately left out others I was not confident of. Confirm the "Active" status on the GST portal before any live demo.

| GSTIN | Company (State) | Expected verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `27AAACR5055K1Z7` | Reliance Industries Limited (Maharashtra) | Valid format, check digit valid; registered legal name should match Reliance Industries Limited; status Active |
| `27AAACT2727Q1ZW` | Tata Motors Limited (Maharashtra) | Valid format, check digit valid; legal name should match Tata Motors; status Active |
| `27AAACR5055K1Z8` | Deliberately mistyped (last character altered from `7` to `8`) | INVALID: check digit fails; should not match any taxpayer; flag as "possible typo, re-verify" |
| `24ABCDE1234F1Z5` | Synthetic placeholder used inside the test documents | Format is valid (15 characters, valid state code 24 = Gujarat) but the check character fails (expected `6`); a strict validator should say INVALID or NOT FOUND |

## 5. Caveats for lawyer reviewers

- The GST notice (07) is drafted under s.73 CGST as requested. In real life, demands for FY 2024-25 onward are issued under s.74A (inserted by the Finance Act 2024), so a sharp reviewer may point that out. Keep it as a bonus finding.
- The s.143(2) notice (08) deliberately omits the date on which the return was filed. A real notice for AY 2025-26 has a statutory service window (3 months from the end of the financial year of filing), so a notice dated 20 Oct 2026 could be time-barred if the return was filed in the normal course. This too is a bonus finding.
- In 09, the contract says 30 days but s.15 caps written payment terms at 45 days; the table uses the 45-day cut-off, which is the conservative reading for the supplier.
- In 10, the "pay within 15 days" date (4 Nov 2026) and the s.106 termination date (30 Nov 2026) are both stated, as is common in Indian practice; the AI should report both.
